def-eigenspace-best-approximation-gap:
## Definition

Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space with a bounded, Hermitian,
coercive form $a$ as in [[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]].
Its energy norm is $\|v\|_a:=\sqrt{a(v,v)}$. Let $E\subseteq V$ be a
nonzero finite-dimensional subspace and let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a
finite-dimensional subspace. Define the directed energy distance and
best-approximation gap by
$$d_a(v,V_h):=\inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|v-w_h\|_a,\qquad \delta_a(E,V_h):=\sup_{\substack{v\in E\\\|v\|_a=1}}d_a(v,V_h).$$
When $E=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}$ is the first $m$
continuous eigenspace directions and $V_h$ is the conforming Galerkin space,
write $\delta_h:=\delta_a(E,V_h)$. This is a directed gap from $E$ to $V_h$;
it does not by itself assert a two-sided gap between two eigenspaces.

The quantity is finite and satisfies $0\le\delta_a(E,V_h)\le1$, since
$0\in V_h$ gives $d_a(v,V_h)\le\|v\|_a$ on the unit sphere.
thm-compact-coercive-form-spectrum-and-m:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an infinite-dimensional
real or complex Hilbert space, let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space over
the same field, and let $J:V\to H$ be an injective, bounded, compact linear
map with dense range ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, Hermitian and coercive with constants
$M,\alpha>0$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]).
Then there is a sequence of eigenpairs $(\lambda_j,e_j)_{j\ge1}$ such that
$$0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots,\qquad \lambda_j\longrightarrow+\infty,$$
where each eigenvalue is repeated according to multiplicity,
$e_j\in V$, $\|Je_j\|_H=1$, and
$$a(e_j,v)=\lambda_j(Je_j,Jv)_H\qquad(v\in V).$$
The vectors $Je_j$ form an orthonormal basis of $H$, and
$e_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ form an orthonormal basis of $V$ for the energy inner
product $a$. In particular, for $v\in V$,
$$\|Jv\|_H^2=\sum_{j\ge1}|(Jv,Je_j)_H|^2,\qquad a(v,v)=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j|(Jv,Je_j)_H|^2,$$
and the Rayleigh quotient $R(v):=a(v,v)/\|Jv\|_H^2$ satisfies the attained
min–max identity
$$\lambda_m=\min_{\substack{S\subseteq V\\\dim S=m}} \max_{v\in S\setminus\{0\}}R(v)\qquad(m\ge1).$$
This is the abstract continuous spectral interface used below. The published
elliptic suppliers on the Dirichlet branch have their own stated domain and
axiom hypotheses; this theorem does not enlarge those imported interfaces.
lem-finite-dimensional-galerkin-minmax:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V_h$ be an
$N$-dimensional subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $V$, with
$N\ge1$. Let $a$ be a bounded Hermitian coercive form on $V$ and let
$b(u,v):=(Ju,Jv)_H$ for a bounded injective linear map $J:V\to H$ into a
Hilbert space. The generalized Ritz problem on $V_h$ is
$$a(u_h,v_h)=\lambda_h b(u_h,v_h)\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
Its eigenvalues, listed with multiplicity in increasing order, are positive
numbers $\lambda_{h,1}\le\cdots\le\lambda_{h,N}$. For every
$1\le m\le N$,
$$\lambda_{h,m}=\min_{\substack{W_h\subseteq V_h\\\dim W_h=m}} \max_{v_h\in W_h\setminus\{0\}} \frac{a(v_h,v_h)}{b(v_h,v_h)}.$$
lem-compact-self-adjoint-residual-contro:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or
complex Hilbert space and let $B_h:H\to H$ be compact and self-adjoint. Put
$$\Sigma_h:=\{0\}\cup\{\nu\ne0:\nu\text{ is an eigenvalue of }B_h\}.$$
Let $\Lambda\subseteq\Sigma_h\setminus\{0\}$ be a finite cluster of
nonzero eigenvalues, let $F$ be the sum of their eigenspaces, and assume
$$\Delta:=\inf\{|\mu-\nu|:\nu\in\Sigma_h\setminus\Lambda\}>0$$
for a real number $\mu$. The compact spectral theorem makes $F$
finite-dimensional. Define the directed Hilbert-space gap by
$$\operatorname{gap}(E,F):=sup_{\substack{u\in E\\\|u\|=1}} \inf_{v\in F}\|u-v\|.$$
If $E\subseteq H$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional subspace and
$$\|(B_h-\mu I)u\|\le\varepsilon\|u\|\qquad(u\in E),$$
then
$$\operatorname{gap}(E,F)\le\varepsilon/\Delta.$$
The estimate compares subspaces and makes no choice of eigenvectors in a
multiple eigenspace.
thm-finite-hermitian-ritz-residual-certi:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A$ be a Hermitian operator on a nonzero
finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space. Let $u$ be a unit vector,
$\mu:=(Au,u)$ its Rayleigh quotient, and
$\rho:=\|(A-\mu I)u\|$. Let $\Sigma(A)$ be the finite set of eigenvalues of
$A$ and, for a nonempty finite set $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, define
$\operatorname{dist}(x,S):=\min_{\nu\in S}|x-\nu|$. Then
$$\operatorname{dist}(\mu,\Sigma(A))\le\rho.$$
If a specified target eigenvalue $\lambda\in\Sigma(A)$ is simple, let $e$ be
any unit eigenvector for it. If $\Sigma(A)\setminus\{\lambda\}$ is nonempty,
assume the certified separation
$$\Delta:=\min_{\nu\in\Sigma(A)\setminus\{\lambda\}}|\mu-\nu|>0.$$
Then the phase-invariant angle satisfies
$$\sin\angle(u,e):=\sqrt{1-| (u,e) |^2}\le\rho/\Delta.$$
If the target is the only eigenvalue, simplicity implies the Hilbert space is
one-dimensional and the angle is zero.
The residual alone does not identify which eigenvalue is nearby, in particular
it does not certify that the target is the lowest eigenvalue.
prop-positive-definite-overlap-whitening:
## Statement

Let $H=H^*\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ be a finite Hermitian stiffness matrix and
let $S=S^*>0$ be a positive-definite overlap or mass matrix. By Cholesky
factorization ([[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]]),
write $S=LL^*$ with $L$ invertible lower triangular and positive diagonal.
Define the whitened Hermitian matrix
$$\widetilde H:=L^{-1}HL^{-*},\qquad L^{-*}:=(L^*)^{-1}.$$
The generalized Ritz equation $Hc=\lambda Sc$ is equivalent under the
invertible change of coordinates $y=L^*c$ to
$\widetilde H y=\lambda y$. The Rayleigh quotients agree:
$$\frac{c^*Hc}{c^*Sc}=\frac{y^*\widetilde H y}{y^*y}\qquad(c\ne0).$$
lem-conforming-energy-projection-is-best:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded,
Hermitian coercive form on $V$, and let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional.
Write $\|v\|_a:=\sqrt{a(v,v)}$ for the induced energy norm.
For each $v\in V$, let $P_hv\in V_h$ be the unique solution of
$$a(P_hv,w_h)=a(v,w_h)\qquad(w_h\in V_h).$$
Then $P_h:V\to V_h$ is linear, $a(v-P_hv,w_h)=0$ for all $w_h\in V_h$, and
$$\|v-P_hv\|_a=\inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|v-w_h\|_a.$$
If $E\subseteq V$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional subspace and
$\delta_a(E,V_h)<1$, then $P_h|_E$ is injective.
lem-conforming-galerkin-ritz-matrix-erro:
## Statement

Assume the compact coercive form setting and notation of
[[thm-compact-coercive-form-spectrum-and-minmax]]. Fix $m\ge1$ and a
finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subseteq V$. Let
$E_m=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}$, let
$\delta_h=\delta_a(E_m,V_h)$ from
[[def-eigenspace-best-approximation-gap]], and let $P_h:V\to V_h$ be the
energy projection of
[[lem-conforming-energy-projection-is-best-approximation]]. For $c\in\mathbb K^m$
write $\|c\|_2=(\sum_i|c_i|^2)^{1/2}$, and for matrices use the induced
Euclidean operator norm $\|M\|_2=\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\|Mc\|_2$
([[def-operator-norm]]). If
$$0\le\delta_h\le\min\left\{\frac12,\sqrt{\frac{\lambda_1}{6m\lambda_m}}\right\},$$
then $P_h|_{E_m}$ is injective. Set $U_h:=P_h(E_m)$. In the energy-orthonormal
basis $p_i=P_h(e_i/\sqrt{\lambda_i})$ of $U_h$, set
$(A_h)_{ij}:=a(p_j,p_i)$ and $(B_h)_{ij}:=(Jp_j,Jp_i)_H$. With
$D_m:=\operatorname{diag}(1/\lambda_1,\ldots,1/\lambda_m)$,
$$\|A_h-I\|_2\le\delta_h^2,\qquad \|B_h-D_m\|_2\le\frac{3m}{\lambda_1}\delta_h^2,$$
and every nonzero $w_h\in U_h$ satisfies
$$\frac{a(w_h,w_h)}{\|Jw_h\|_H^2} \le\lambda_m+C_m\delta_h^2, \qquad C_m:=2\lambda_m+\frac{6m\lambda_m^2}{\lambda_1}.$$
thm-conforming-galerkin-eigenvalue-upper:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the compact coercive form setting of
[[thm-compact-coercive-form-spectrum-and-minmax]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be
finite-dimensional, let $m\ge1$ with $\dim V_h\ge m$, and let
$E_m=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}$ be the first $m$ continuous
eigen-directions. Write $\delta_h=\delta_a(E_m,V_h)$ as in
[[def-eigenspace-best-approximation-gap]]. There are $\delta_0>0$ and
$C_m<\infty$, depending only on $m$ and the first $m$ continuous eigenvalues,
such that if $\delta_h\le\delta_0$, then the $m$th conforming Ritz value
$\lambda_{h,m}$ satisfies
$$\lambda_m\le\lambda_{h,m}\le\lambda_m+C_m\delta_h^2.$$
The lower bound holds for every conforming $V_h$ of dimension at least $m$;
the upper error bound requires the stated small-gap condition. More generally,
let $a_0$ be a Hermitian lower-bounded form on the same $V$, and suppose a
specified shift $\sigma$ makes
$a_\sigma(u,v):=a_0(u,v)+\sigma(Ju,Jv)_H$ bounded, Hermitian and coercive,
with the same injective compact dense map $J$. Define $\delta_h^\sigma$ using
the energy norm $\|v\|_{a_\sigma}:=\sqrt{a_\sigma(v,v)}$ and the first $m$
eigenspace directions for $a_\sigma$. The theorem applies to the shifted
problem with $\delta_h^\sigma$; its continuous and discrete eigenvalues are
the corresponding unshifted eigenvalues plus $\sigma$. Subtracting $\sigma$
preserves their ordering and the difference $\lambda_{h,m}-\lambda_m$.
thm-conforming-galerkin-eigenspace-gap-u:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the compact coercive form setting of
[[thm-compact-coercive-form-spectrum-and-minmax]]. Suppose a continuous
eigenvalue $\lambda$ occupies the isolated cluster of indices
$r,\ldots,s$, so $\lambda_r=\cdots=\lambda_s=\lambda$ and
$\lambda_{s+1}>\lambda$, with $\lambda_{r-1}<\lambda$ when $r>1$. Let
$E:=\operatorname{span}\{e_r,\ldots,e_s\}$,
$E_s:=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_s\}$, and let
$V_h\subseteq V$ be conforming with $\dim V_h\ge s$. Put
$\delta_s:=\delta_a(E_s,V_h)$ using
[[def-eigenspace-best-approximation-gap]]. If $\delta_s$ is sufficiently
small that the eigenvalue theorem
[[thm-conforming-galerkin-eigenvalue-upper-bound-quadratic-gap-error]] applies
at index $s$ and, when $r>1$, at index $r-1$, and
$C_s\delta_s^2<\tfrac12(\lambda_{s+1}-\lambda)$ and, when $r>1$,
$C_{r-1}\delta_s^2<\tfrac12(\lambda-\lambda_{r-1})$, then
the discrete Ritz eigenspace $E_h$ associated with indices $r,\ldots,s$ has
dimension $s-r+1$ and
$$\delta_a(E,E_h)\le C_{r,s,\lambda}\,\delta_s.$$
This compares the invariant subspaces across the whole repeated eigenvalue;
it does not select individual eigenvectors inside the cluster.
